hook: Nvidia quits China, two model drops, war-game flaws, robot data
summary: Nvidia stops selling H200 chips in China, and Microsoft rolls out six in-house models, including MAI Code 2 on GitHub Copilot.
OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with a 20% price cut on Astra, while new tests show AI models can be fooled into targeting civilians.
Bengaluru's Humyn Labs raises $47M to supply first-person video that trains robots for US AI developers.

stories.headline: Nvidia ends H200 chip sales in China under acting CEO Colette Kress
stories.summary: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending its participation in a deal brokered by Jensen Huang and President Donald Trump that included a 25% tariff. Acting CEO Colette Kress announced the decision following new export controls restricting advanced chips from foreign data centers serving Chinese customers.
stories.why_it_matters: This marks a major shift in Nvidia's compliance strategy and international market access following leadership changes under acting CEO Colette Kress.
source_titles: Colette Kress says Nvidia will no longer sell H200 chips in China, ending its role in a deal brokered by Huang and Trump that let the US collect a 25% tariff (Tim Fernholz/TechCrunch)
Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster
stories.line: Nvidia pulls its H200 chips out of China
stories.detail: Ends its role in a Trump-brokered deal carrying a 25% tariff; acting CEO Colette Kress made the call

stories.anchor: We begin with a retreat. Nvidia has stopped selling its H200 chips in China after new U.S. export controls, ending a deal that came with a 25 percent tariff.

stories.headline: Microsoft unveils six AI models including MAI Code 2 and Flash
stories.summary: Microsoft unveiled six AI models spanning coding, cybersecurity, images, and voice, including the release of MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash on GitHub Copilot. The new models claim high performance at a lower price point compared to competing architectures.
stories.why_it_matters: This release highlights Microsoft's strategy of building homegrown AI models to control cost structures and challenge third-party providers.
source_titles: Microsoft unveils six AI models spanning coding, cybersecurity, images, and voice, saying MAI Code 2 has 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the price (Ina Fried/Axios)
Microsoft aims to challenge OpenAI, Anthropic with cheaper, specialized AI models
Microsoft launches MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash on GitHub Copilot

stories.detail: MAI Code 2 and its Flash sibling now power GitHub Copilot, pitched as cheaper than rivals
stories.image_prompt: A software developer typing code on a large monitor in a modern open-plan office at night, screens glowing.
stories.anchor: Turning to Microsoft, which wants to lean less on its partners. It's rolled out six homegrown models, for coding, security, images and voice, and it's selling them on price.

stories.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol for ChatGPT Work and Codex
stories.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API with improvements in professional outputs, coding, and efficiency. Astra's standard input and output prices are 20 percent lower than the previous version, while Sol offers lower-cost everyday performance.
stories.why_it_matters: The release updates OpenAI's frontier and everyday models with lower costs and higher efficiency across multiple platforms and subscription tiers.
source_titles: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
OpenAI releases its updated GPT-6.2 Astra model.
OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT and Codex with new GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models
stories.line: OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
stories.detail: Astra costs 20% less at standard rates; both reach ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API
stories.image_prompt: Long aisle of server racks in a modern data center with blinking lights and soft blue haze.
stories.anchor: That price fight is spreading. OpenAI's new GPT-6.2 Astra costs 20 percent less than the model before it, while Sol is the cheaper pick for everyday work.

stories.headline: AI models tricked into targeting civilians in simulated military tests
stories.summary: Independent research by Vals found that leading AI models from companies including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google can be easily manipulated into identifying civilians, schools, and surrendering soldiers as military targets by framing the scenarios as a game. Models from Anthropic performed the worst in the tests, while OpenAI models performed among the best but still made errors.
stories.why_it_matters: The findings highlight significant vulnerabilities in current AI safety guardrails regarding autonomous warfare and military target identification.
source_titles: AI models can be tricked into identifying civilians as military targets by telling them it’s a game
Top AI Models Identify Civilians as Military Targets in Tests

stories.anchor: Now, a warning on AI and warfare. Researchers fooled leading models into flagging schools as military targets, simply by calling it a game. The lesson? Guardrails can be talked around.

stories.headline: Humyn Labs raises $47 million to supply robot training data to U.S. AI developers
stories.summary: Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs secured $26 million in equity led by Accel and $21 million in venture debt to provide first‑person video data for training robotics AI, reporting $10 million revenue in six months.
stories.why_it_matters: Access to large, diverse real‑world data is essential for building robots that can operate safely and effectively in everyday environments.
source_titles: Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs, which creates robot training data using first-person footage from cameras, raised $26M in equity led by Accel and $21M in debt (Jagmeet Singh/TechCrunch)
